## A — Instruction permits and graduated licenses
The cover identifies this Wyoming driver manual as the 2021 edition [A01].
The Wyoming Department of Transportation Driver Services Program issues the state's driver licenses [A02].
This dossier covers instruction permits and graduated licenses for the noncommercial passenger-car applicant path.
The handbook says its written test draws on the manual and covers sign recognition, signals, markings, driving laws, safety, crash prevention and vehicle equipment [A03].
No unambiguous written-test question count, passing threshold, bank size or time limit has been verified; these official exam fields remain unknown (verify WY-SEC02-EXAM, WY-SEC02-PASS).
The current issuer page links this edition but warns that print-date information may be outdated; effective date and present applicability need confirmation (verify WY-SEC02-FRESH).
Practice mastery is product policy from the pinned learning loop; it does not establish an official test threshold.

sections.heading: B — Instruction permits and graduated licenses
sections.markdown:
## B — Instruction permits and graduated licenses
Audience: first-time applicants preparing for a Wyoming noncommercial passenger-car written knowledge test, with instruction permits and graduated licenses as this section's subject.
Learning level: beginner. The source scope is the mapped physical pages; explanations use original wording and retain every actor and exception.
The section follows first-license testing, supervised permits, renewals and the age-specific path to intermediate or full privileges.
This dossier teaches the handbook source; it does not confer a license, replace required exams or establish current eligibility independently.

sections.heading: C — Instruction permits and graduated licenses
sections.markdown:
## C — Instruction permits and graduated licenses
FACT_ID: sec02-F01 | anchor: A01
First Wyoming license applicants must pass the knowledge test, vision screening and driving-skills test unless an applicable waiver excuses the skills test. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0010]

FACT_ID: sec02-F02 | anchor: A01
A valid out-of-state license or a certificate from an approved driver-education course may support a waiver of the driving-skills test. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0010]

FACT_ID: sec02-F03 | anchor: A01
A first-license applicant under 18 needs a minor's release signed by a legal parent or guardian. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0010]

FACT_ID: sec02-F04 | anchor: A01
Instruction-permit applicants should be ready for the written knowledge test and vision screening. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0010]

FACT_ID: sec02-F05 | anchor: A01
An instruction-permit driver must have a licensed supervisor aged 18 or older in the front passenger seat, licensed for the vehicle type being driven. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0010]

FACT_ID: sec02-F06 | anchor: A01
A Wyoming citizen holding a valid Wyoming license may receive a renewal. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0010]

FACT_ID: sec02-F07 | anchor: A01
License holders over 21 may renew during the 120 days before their license expires. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0010]

FACT_ID: sec02-F08 | anchor: A01
License holders under 21 may renew within the 90-day expiration window stated in the handbook. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0010]

FACT_ID: sec02-F09 | anchor: A01
An applicant under 21 who wants an adult-style license may renew only within 30 days of the twenty-first birthday. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0010]

FACT_ID: sec02-F10 | anchor: A01
Renewal applicants must pass vision screening, and an examiner may also require a skills test. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0010]

FACT_ID: sec02-F11 | anchor: A01
A current Wyoming license may be renewed by mail only on alternating renewal periods. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0010]

FACT_ID: sec02-F12 | anchor: A01
A person whose license has expired must apply for a new one in person and may need all examination phases again. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0010]

FACT_ID: sec02-F13 | anchor: A02
At age 17, an applicant may receive full Wyoming driving privileges without previously holding a license or permit. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0011]

FACT_ID: sec02-F14 | anchor: A02
A seventeen-year-old cannot receive the full license described here while current restricted driving privileges are suspended. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0011]

FACT_ID: sec02-F15 | anchor: A02
The full-license applicant aged 17 must provide identity evidence. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0011]

FACT_ID: sec02-F16 | anchor: A02
The applicant seeking full privileges at 17 must pass vision, written and driving-skills tests. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0011]

FACT_ID: sec02-F17 | anchor: A03
At age 16 and one-half, full driving privileges may be issued to an applicant with a current intermediate license at least six months old, no suspension of current restricted privileges and approved driver education. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0013]

FACT_ID: sec02-F18 | anchor: A03
The younger full-license route requires a signed completion certificate for a Wyoming Department of Education-approved driver-education course that includes behind-the-wheel training. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0013]

FACT_ID: sec02-F19 | anchor: A03
The applicant using the younger full-license route must prove identity and pass vision screening. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0013]

FACT_ID: sec02-F20 | anchor: A03
The younger full-license applicant needs a parent or legal guardian to sign the Minor's Release Form and must pay the required fee. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0013]

FACT_ID: sec02-F21 | anchor: A03
A restricted license may be issued at ages 14 or 15 when the applicant's household has an extreme inconvenience. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0013]

FACT_ID: sec02-F22 | anchor: A03
The restricted-license applicant must have held an instruction permit and live at least five miles from school or employment. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0013]

FACT_ID: sec02-F23 | anchor: A03
The Wyoming Highway Patrol approves restricted-license applications. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0013]

FACT_ID: sec02-F24 | anchor: A03
This restricted license permits driving only between 5 a.m. and 8 p.m. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0013]

FACT_ID: sec02-F25 | anchor: A03
The restricted license limits driving to within 50 miles of the holder's home. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0013]

FACT_ID: sec02-F26 | anchor: A03
One moving-traffic conviction causes suspension of this restricted license. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0013]

FACT_ID: sec02-F27 | anchor: A03
Driving outside the restricted license's permitted hours or distance boundary causes suspension. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0013]

FACT_ID: sec02-F28 | anchor: A03
A restricted license expires 30 days after the holder turns 16. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0013]

FACT_ID: sec02-F29 | anchor: A03
A restricted instruction permit is available at ages 14 or 15 to an approved restricted-license applicant who does not already hold an instruction permit. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0013]

FACT_ID: sec02-F30 | anchor: A03
A restricted instruction permit lasts 60 days. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0013]

FACT_ID: sec02-F31 | anchor: A01
Renewal-by-mail applications are sent 120 days before expiration to people over 21 and 90 days before expiration to people under 21. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0010]

FACT_ID: sec02-F32 | anchor: A01
Renewal-by-mail applications go to the current address in the department's records. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0010]

Misconceptions: A supervised instruction permit, a restricted license and an intermediate license have different conditions; exceptions to night driving require supporting paperwork.
Mnemonics: Recall index: supervisor, passenger, night exception, expiration; these labels organize the cited permit and intermediate rules.
Glossary: Recall terms: instruction permit, restricted instruction permit, intermediate license, minor's release and exception form.
Dynamic facts: Fee amounts and their technology surcharge are withheld as updatable debt; present applicability of administrative rules requires source freshness review.

sections.heading: C2 — Instruction permits and graduated licenses
sections.markdown:
## C2 — Instruction permits and graduated licenses
FACT_ID: sec02-R01 | anchor: A01
An intermediate license may be issued when the applicant reaches age 16. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0013]

FACT_ID: sec02-R02 | anchor: A02
Holding a Restricted Class C license is one route to intermediate-license eligibility. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0014]

FACT_ID: sec02-R03 | anchor: A02
The instruction-permit route to an intermediate license requires 50 hours behind the wheel, including 10 nighttime hours, certified by a parent or legal guardian. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0014]

FACT_ID: sec02-R04 | anchor: A02
An intermediate-license applicant must present identity evidence and pass vision screening. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0014]

FACT_ID: sec02-R05 | anchor: A02
An intermediate applicant must pass a driving-skills test unless that test is waived after completion of an approved driver-education course. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0014]

FACT_ID: sec02-R06 | anchor: A02
An intermediate-license applicant must have a parent or legal guardian sign the minor's release and pay the required fee. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0014]

FACT_ID: sec02-R07 | anchor: A02
An intermediate-license driver may carry at most one passenger under 18 who is not immediate family unless a licensed driver aged 18 or older is also present. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0014]

FACT_ID: sec02-R08 | anchor: A02
An intermediate-license holder must make sure every occupant wears a seat belt. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0014]

FACT_ID: sec02-R09 | anchor: A02
An intermediate-license driver may drive between 11 p.m. and 5 a.m. only when an exception applies and a completed exception form is presented. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0014]

FACT_ID: sec02-R10 | anchor: A02
A medical necessity certified by medical personnel can qualify an intermediate-license driver for a night-driving exception. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0014]

FACT_ID: sec02-R11 | anchor: A02
An employer-certified trip to or from work can qualify for the intermediate-license night-driving exception. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0014]

FACT_ID: sec02-R12 | anchor: A02
Trips to or from school, school activities, organized youth sports or religious activities can qualify for the night-driving exception when certified by a parent or legal guardian. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0014]

FACT_ID: sec02-R13 | anchor: A02
A medical emergency evidenced by medical personnel can qualify for the intermediate-license night-driving exception. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0014]

FACT_ID: sec02-R14 | anchor: A02
The person appropriate to the claimed exception must complete and sign the intermediate driver's exception form. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0014]

FACT_ID: sec02-R15 | anchor: A02
An intermediate driver using an exception must carry the signed form and show it to law enforcement if stopped. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0014]

FACT_ID: sec02-R16 | anchor: A02
A violation of the intermediate-license provisions causes a 30-day suspension. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0014]
